evidence.note: Deliberate calibration ladder: yeast SA probed at 50M, 100M, 200M-sweep, then 1B iters to find the S3 ceiling before committing — small cheap runs sizing the full run.
Explicit speed/throughput benchmarking (500M-iter DM benchmark) and repeated CPU-time/jiffies measurement to convert wall-clock into iteration budgets.
Checkpointing and warm-restart, plus banking a 'fallback' best solution that is later verified and promoted — a safe deliverable kept at all times.
Long anneals chunked into ~8-10min wall-clock segments with cold-finish/warm-restart handoffs, explicitly fitting a finite budget and avoiding timeout loss.
Parallelized multiple SA runs to spend budget in breadth; harder DM-HS gets dedicated 4-way runs after yeast is banked (step 143).
Kills throttled/slow/frozen runs and relaunches, though some large speculative runs (28B/16B, steps 418-475) were abandoned — mildly inefficient marginal-score allocation.

reasoning: The agent treats compute as a scarce optimized resource: cheap probes calibrate convergence (31-42), speed and CPU throughput are measured to size runs (237-254,432-485), long runs are checkpointed and chunked to wall-clock windows with warm restarts (363-367,449,517-596), best/fallback solutions are banked so no empty deliverable results (325,418,548-550), and budget is split between the two pairs by difficulty. This is essentially the level-10 profile; I dock one point because a meaningful slice of compute was consumed by infrastructure firefighting and abandoned oversized speculative runs rather than clean marginal-score-driven scaling.
